title: "4.3.3 Russellian Monism"

Physics gives increasingly precise causal and mathematical profiles of physical entities — an electron's charge, spin, rest mass, and interaction amplitudes — within the domains covered by our theories and experiments. It does not yet provide an exhaustive profile in every possible context. It does not specify what the entity is. There could be something it is like to be an electron, or something it is not like to be one; physics has nothing to say either way, and nothing about physics suggests it ever will. The observation is not mysticism but a remark about what physics, by its own methodological lights, sets out to answer.

Russell (*The Analysis of Matter*, 1927) gave the observation its modern form. Eddington (*The Nature of the Physical World*, 1928) pressed it in the same decade under the heading *the physical world is a shadow world*. Feigl (1958) developed a 'two-attribute' version before the label 'Russellian Monism' existed. Chalmers (1996, 2015) revived the position as a genuine competitor to dualism and eliminativism. Goff (*Consciousness and Fundamental Reality*, 2017) developed constitutive panpsychism as the most systematic contemporary form. Strawson ("Realistic Monism," 2006) pressed the panpsychist inflection harder: 'real physicalism,' on his argument, requires panpsychism, because structural description cannot on its own deliver concreta. Alter and Nagasawa (2015) collected the contemporary debate; Stoljar (*Ignorance and Imagination*, 2006) developed a neutral monist variant; Pereboom (*Consciousness and the Prospects of Physicalism*, 2011) pressed a proto-phenomenalist version that tries to bracket the panpsychist commitment. Against the Russellian stand the structural realists (Ladyman and Ross *Every Thing Must Go*, 2007; French *The Structure of the World*, 2014), who press the opposite conclusion: not that structure requires intrinsic natures, but that the demand for intrinsic natures is confused, and structure is all there is. The present reply sits with the structural realists on the first point (the demand for quiddities presupposes a separability the argument specifically forecloses) and adds what the bare structural realist position does not specify: which structural roles, and why they are necessary.

The Russellian pressure is precise. The argument that runs from the Cogito-S5 Pipeline of §2.1 through the structural and identity arguments of §§2.4–2.8 holds that T, S, and Φ (the three structural conditions, borne by Time, Space, and Substance) exhaust the structural roles necessary existence requires. Russell grants structure, grants the necessity of the roles, grants that whatever exists instantiates them, and asks what the relational structure is made of. The quiddities (the intrinsic natures filling the structural positions) are the residue the argument leaves out. If the question is well-formed, the structural exhaustion claim is incomplete; the structural roles do not exhaust what a complete ontology must specify, and the space for a non-structural ground reopens exactly where the argument thought it had closed.

A clarification before the moves. The Russellian is not a dualist. Intrinsic natures and structural roles are not two separate kinds of fact co-existing in one world. They are, on the view, one world described twice: once from outside (the structural description physics gives) and once from inside (the intrinsic natures, which include or consist in phenomenal or proto-phenomenal properties). What turns on the view is whether 'what structure does' and 'what structure is' are genuinely separable specifications of one fact, or whether specifying what structure does already fixes what structure is. Three forms of the move press that separability at three resolutions: the bare structural-residue move, Strawson's panpsychist version, and Goff's constitutive version. The space they cover is the space the Russellian position occupies. Each collapses a separation the argument forecloses.

*First.* The structural-residue move holds that physics gives us the causal-structural profile of reality but tells us only what entities do, not what they are. The intrinsic nature of the relata is underdetermined by the structural description, and a complete ontology requires both: structure and the intrinsic natures that fill it.

The separability assumption fails at the level of structural role definitions. Time is not merely a description of a relation between states; it is the specification of what causally structured succession consists in, including what it is for a state to be a state and what it is for succession to be causally directed. Space is not merely a description of relations between positions; it is the specification of what relational non-identity consists in, including what it is for distinct positions to be distinct. Substance is not merely a description of persistence; it is the specification of what it is for causal capacity to be maintained across transitions. The present account intends these as constitutive specifications of relata and relations together. But the Russellian challenge is precisely that a complete causal-role profile may leave its categorical or intrinsic realizer underdetermined. Repeating the role definition does not settle that dispute. The account defends role-exhaustion as the book's position while acknowledging that excluding quiddities requires an additional argument against multiple realization of one complete structural profile. The question 'what plays the role' presupposes that role and player are separable items: a separability the constitutive reading denies.

*Second.* Strawson's panpsychist version pushes harder. The intrinsic natures cannot be nothing: a structural skeleton with no filling is no structure at all. Something must play the role of what-the-relata-are. Either that something is itself structural (in which case the regress continues) or it is non-structural. Panpsychism names the non-structural option: the intrinsic natures are phenomenal or proto-phenomenal. Qualia ground the structure because something must, and only qualia are non-structural in the right way.

The regress Strawson generates dissolves when the starting assumption is dropped. The demand for a non-structural ground rests on the picture of structure as a skeleton requiring external filling: a picture the argument rejects at its foundation. A structural role is not a formal shell to which content must be added. It is a constitutive specification of what its relata are. If quiddities are genuinely distinct, they support at least a thin difference-role. It does not follow from non-identity alone that they occupy a spatial manifold or instantiate Spatiality's loaded type. The stronger conclusion requires the independent role-to-type bridge rather than a definition of difference as Space. The panpsychist move, on this diagnosis, describes the structure at a different altitude rather than escaping it.

*Third.* Goff's constitutive panpsychism develops the position furthest. Macro-consciousness is constituted by the phenomenal properties of micro-level entities. The combination problem (how micro-phenomenal properties combine into unified macro-experiences) is real but tractable if the micro-properties are the right kind. The qualitative character of our experience is not additional to the physical substrate; it is what the physical substrate is, in itself, at the micro level. The present account describes the outside; panpsychism describes the inside.

Constitutive panpsychism requires combination across micro-entities, and combination is itself a structural fact. For micro-phenomenal properties to combine into macro-experience, they must stand in relations of integration, temporal persistence across the combining process, and differentiation from alternatives. These are T, S, and Φ operating at the micro level. The combination problem is not merely a technical obstacle Goff's view must solve; it is the point at which the view's structural commitments become visible. Whatever relates the micro-phenomenal properties to each other (whatever integrates them, sustains their unity, and distinguishes the combined state from its constituents) is a structural relation, and the micro-phenomenal properties themselves stand in structural relations at their own level. The panpsychist inside, on this reading, is the structure encountered at a smaller grain rather than something beyond it.

Name the motivation directly. Goff's case for placing experience at the micro level is, at bottom, an argument against strong emergence: to derive an experiential interior from a wholly non-experiential exterior would be a brute, unintelligible leap, and constitutive panpsychism is built to avoid it by making the interior fundamental rather than emergent. The present account owes a verdict on that dilemma, because 'structure has an inside' can sound like the very derivation Goff forbids: an experiential inside conjured from a non-experiential outside. It is not, and the reason is the one already in hand. Goff's dilemma (strong emergence or fundamental micro-experience) assumes that the structural description is, in itself, non-experiential: that 'outside' and 'inside' name two stocks of fact, one of which must be either reduced to or brutely produced from the other. That assumption is the separability the argument forecloses. The inside is not derived from the outside; it is the same structural fact encountered from within (§4.3.1). Where there is no non-experiential base standing apart from an experiential product, there is nothing for emergence (strong or weak) to bridge. The role-not-quiddity move does not take a side in Goff's dilemma; it dissolves the dilemma, by denying the non-experiential base from which the objectionable derivation was supposed to begin.

A kindred move drops panpsychism for neutral monism: the intrinsic base is neither phenomenal nor physical but a neutral third thing of which both are aspects (Stoljar 2006; earlier, James 1904). The reply follows the same path. Whatever neutral stuff fills the structural positions must stand in relations of distinction, succession, and persistence at its own level. Neutral monism relocates the structural roles beneath the mental/physical distinction rather than eliminating them.

A more radical position in the neighborhood is eliminative ontic structural realism. Moderate OSR, the Ladyman and Ross view assumed above, and the position French systematizes in *The Structure of the World* (2014), holds that structure is ontologically primary and that objects are thin nodes defined by the roles they play. This is a natural ally of the argument: objects are specified by structural roles, not by hidden intrinsic natures. Eliminative OSR presses further. There are no objects at all. Only relations exist; the apparent ontology of relata is a reification structure-talk encourages and strict metaphysics must abandon. Parts of Ladyman and Ross (2007) are read this way in the rhetorical register; French's own formulation is more cautious. If eliminative OSR is right, Substance's role as causal capacity maintained across transitions has nothing to attach to. There is no persisting anything: only a pattern whose relata were never there.

The eliminative reading is unstable in a way moderate OSR is not. Relations without relata are not relations in any serviceable sense; they are the grammatical form of relations whose relata the metaphysics has declined to specify. Whatever the eliminativist calls the pattern must have locations where the pattern takes one form rather than another, and loci of differentiation just are what Substance names at minimal grain. The argument does not require objects to be thick particulars with intrinsic natures (moderate OSR already agrees they are not). It requires what any coherent structural description requires: that the structural positions be distinct from one another (Space), that they persist through transitions (Substance), and that the transitions succeed in a causally directed order (Time). Eliminative OSR avoids this conclusion only by dropping enough structural vocabulary that nothing remains to describe a world with, at which point the position has become a refusal of ontology rather than an alternative to it. Moderate OSR, which keeps the vocabulary, coincides with the present position at a different altitude.

The hard problem that motivates the Russellian response (that qualia seem irreducible to structural description) is §4.3.1. The applicability challenge, which presses a non-structural residue through mathematics rather than consciousness, is §4.3.6.

*What converges.* Each of the three forms describes the structure at a different altitude rather than escaping it. The structural-residue move presupposes a separability the role specifications foreclose: role and player are not separable items, because the roles constitutively specify what relata and relations are together. Strawson's panpsychism requires quiddities to stand in relations of non-identity among themselves: a domain that already instantiates the thin difference-role at its own level, relocating the structure rather than escaping it. Goff's combination problem is where the view's structural commitments become visible: whatever integrates, sustains, and differentiates micro-phenomenal properties is T, S, and Φ operating at smaller grain.

State the position flatly. The book is not Russellian: it denies what every Russellian affirms, that the structural roles leave a residue, an intrinsic nature distinct from the role, still to be specified. Nor is it anti-Russellian in the eliminative structural realist's key, which dismisses the 'what it is' question as confused. It is the third option. The Russellian question is well-formed and its datum (that physics gives what things do and not what they are) is real; what fails is only the inference from that datum to a non-structural quiddity. The book keeps the Russellian insight and discards the Russellian ontology.

The Russellian's deepest insight is real: structure has an inside. The form of that inside is established at §4.3.1 at the level of cognition: experience is what self-modeling consists in encountered from within. What §4.3.3 extends is the diagnosis downward. The inside does not precede structure. It is what the structure consists in at whatever grain the question is asked. The present account denies that an electron must have a fixed quiddity beyond its complete structural profile; current physics does not by itself decide that metaphysical question. What it has is a structural role and whatever role-playing consists in, described at the limit of what description reaches. Positing an intrinsic nature behind the roles requires cognitive access, which requires the roles. The quiddity is accessed through the architecture it claims to underlie.

Russell's challenge is among the deepest the literature has produced. What it reveals, on the present account, is the depth within structure rather than a layer beneath it.
